units.text: This annex defines the syntax of TTCN-3 using extended BNF (henceforth just called BNF).
Table A.1 defines the metanotation used to specify the extended BNF grammar for TTCN-3.
Table A.1: The syntactic metanotation
::= is defined to be definition of non-terminal abc xyz abc followed by xyz concatenation
alternative alternative

[abc] 0 or 1 instances of abc optional {abc} 0 or more instances of abc repetition 1 {abc}+ 1 or more instances of abc repetition 2 {abc}#(n, m) n to m instances of abc repetition 3 (...) textual grouping grouping Abc the non-terminal symbol abc non-terminal "abc" a terminal symbol abc terminal
NOTE: The metanotation defined in table A.1 is parsed from left to right.

The metanotation operators have the following precedence, from highest (binding tightest) at the top, to lowest (loosest) at the bottom: Repetition, Optional Grouping Concatenation Alternative Definition
In general all TTCN-3 language constructs (i.e. definitions, declarations, statements and operations) are terminated with a semi-colon (;).

The semi-colon is optional if the language construct ends with a right-hand curly brace (}) or the following symbol is a right-hand curly brace (}), i.e. the language construct is the last statement in a statement block.
In TTCN-3, all comma-separated lists are terminated with a right hand brace (")"), a right-hand curly brace ("}"), a left-hand curly brace ("{") or a semi-colon (";").

In addition TTCN-3 allows optional trailing commas in comma-separated lists with a variable number of items, i.e. an optional comma is allowed immediately before the closing right hand brace (")") or a right-hand curly brace (}) of a list or before the start of the next lexical symbol indicated by a left-hand curly brace ("{") or a semi-colon (";").
TTCN-3 identifiers are case sensitive and shall only contain lowercase letters (a-z) uppercase letters (A-Z), numeric digits (0-9) and the underscore ( _ ) symbol.
An identifier shall begin with a letter (i.e. not with a number and not an underscore).
::=: abc xyz; is defined to be: abc followed by xyz; definition of non-terminal: concatenation
::=: alternative; is defined to be: alternative
::=: [abc]; is defined to be: 0 or 1 instances of abc; definition of non-terminal: optional
::=: {abc}; is defined to be: 0 or more instances of abc; definition of non-terminal: repetition 1
::=: {abc}+; is defined to be: 1 or more instances of abc; definition of non-terminal: repetition 2
::=: {abc}#(n, m); is defined to be: n to m instances of abc; definition of non-terminal: repetition 3
::=: (...); is defined to be: textual grouping; definition of non-terminal: grouping
::=: Abc; is defined to be: the non-terminal symbol abc; definition of non-terminal: non-terminal
::=: "abc"; is defined to be: a terminal symbol abc; definition of non-terminal: terminal
NOTE: The metanotation defined in table A.1 is parsed from left to right.

The metanotation operators have the following precedence, from highest (binding tightest) at the top, to lowest (loosest) at the bottom: Repetition, Optional Grouping Concatenation Alternative Definition
::=; is defined to be; definition of non-terminal
Comments written in free text may appear anywhere in a TTCN-3 specification.
Comments may contain any graphical character defined in ISO/IEC 10646 [2].
Block comments shall be opened by the symbol pair /* and closed by the symbol pair */.
EXAMPLE 1:

/* This is a block comment 
  spread over two lines */
Block comments shall not be nested.
/* This is not /* a legal */ comment */
Line comments shall be opened by the symbol pair // and closed by a <newline> or <end-of-file>.
EXAMPLE 2:

// This is a line comment
  // spread over two lines

Table A.3: List of TTCN-3 terminals which are reserved words

action fail noblock select activate false none self address float not send alive for not_a_number sender all friend not4b set alt from nowait setencode altstep function null setverdict and signature and4b getverdict octetstring start any getcall of stop anytype getreply omit subset goto on superset bitstring group optional system boolean or break halt or4b template hexstring out testcase case override timeout call if timer catch ifpresent param to char import pass trigger charstring in pattern true check inconc permutation type clear infinity port complement inout present union component integer private universal connect interleave procedure unmap const isbound public continue ischosen value control ispresent raise valueof create isvalue read var receive variant deactivate kill record verdicttype decmatch killed recursive default rem while disconnect label repeat with display language reply do length return xor done log running xor4b runs else map encode match enumerated message error mixed except mod exception modifies execute module extends modulepar extension mtc external
The TTCN-3 terminals listed in table A.3 shall not be used as identifiers in a TTCN-3 module.
These terminals shall be written in all lowercase letters.
Additionally, there are special TTCN-3 terminals consisting of an @-symbol, directly followed by an identifier.
These terminals shall also be written in all lowercase letters.
NOTE: These terminals can be used in combination with the @-symbol, which results in a specific semantics for the annotated language element.
They can also be used like any other identifier without any special meaning.

@abstract @decoded @index @nocase @control @default @lazy @nodefault @deterministic @local @fuzzy
Table A.5: List of TTCN-3 terminals which are reserved words in extension packages

apply history par assert prev timestamp at implies inv realtime until configuration conjunct mode seq values cont setstate notinv static wait delta now stepsize disjunct stream duration object onentry finished onexit
The TTCN-3 terminals listed in table A.5 are used as keywords inside the TTCN-3 extension packages.
These terminals shall not be used as identifiers in a TTCN-3 module.
These terminals shall be written in all lowercase letters.

The elements of the TTCN-3 syntax (reserved words, identifiers, terminal symbols and literal values) shall be separated by whitespace or by special terminal symbols listed in table A.2 according to the TTCN-3 syntax.
In representing whitespace, any one or more of the following characters of the C0 set of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] and of annex A of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] may be used in any combination:
HT - HORIZONTAL TABULATION (9)
LF - LINE FEED (10)
VT -VERTICAL TABULATION (11)
FF - FORM FEED (12)
CR - CARRIAGE RETURN (13)
SP - SPACE (32)
The characters of the C0 set of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] and of annex A of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] below are denoting newline (end of line).
A single CR(13) character directly followed by an LF(10) character denote a single end of line (i.e. the sequence CRLFCRLFVT denotes 3 lines):
LF - LINE FEED (10)
VT - VERTICAL TABULATION (11)
FF - FORM FEED (12)
CR - CARRIAGE RETURN (13)
Any character or character sequence that is a valid newline is also a valid whitespace.
@abstract @control; @decoded @default @deterministic @fuzzy; @index @lazy @local; @nocase @nodefault

NOTE: It is recommended that for newline only the CR and LF and for whitespace only the HT, LF, CR and SP control characters are used as the VT and FF characters may cause problems with some conventional text editors.
